name: argmax-two-rows-of-ten-signed-chars-an-unsigned-accumulator-gets-wrong
rationale:
No authored case reached `llvm.smax.i8`, which 3 corpus sources use; this kernel is MLX's `arg_reduce_general<char, ArgMax, 4>` and the call IS its running maximum, so its answer decides both output words. The case runs two rows of ten with `ndim` 1, `shape` (2), `in_strides` (10), `out_strides` (1), `axis_stride` 1 and `axis_size` 10: two threadgroups of thirty-two threads, so threads 0..31 reduce row 0 -- where `gid < lsize` short-circuits `elem_to_loc` and both offsets are 0 -- and threads 32..63 reduce row 1, where both index loops actually run. Each thread reads four consecutive axis elements, so with an axis of ten only threads 0, 1 and 2 see real data and the other twenty-nine see nothing but the identity the out-of-range guard supplies.

Signedness is the case, and its counterfactual is stated exactly: the running accumulator is the only thing `llvm.smax.i8` decides -- the index test beside it and the comparison in the cross-lane reduction are `icmp` and stay signed whatever the call lowers to. Simulating this kernel with the accumulator replaced by an unsigned maximum and everything else unchanged answers indices 2 and 7 where the correct lowering answers 4 and 3. Both rows separate, and they separate differently: row 0 is 3, -1, 2, -2, 7, -3, 5, -9, -8, -6, mixed-sign small values whose maximum is 7 at index 4 while the unsigned maximum latches onto a negative early; row 1 is 7, -100, 120, 127, 0, -1, 127, 5, -3, 12, where the true answer is the first of two equal extrema. Row 1's repeat -- 127 at indices 3 and 6 -- is also the tie rule: the per-thread scan advances its index only on a STRICT improvement and the simd reduction prefers the smaller index on an equal value, so 3 is the only correct answer and 6 is exactly what a non-strict comparison gives.

The extrema sit in different threads' four-element windows -- row 0's in thread 1, row 1's in thread 0 with a runner-up in thread 1 -- so the cross-lane `air.simd_shuffle_down.s.i8` pair reduction has to run for either row to come out right. The input buffer carries four elements past the two rows that the `axis_size` guard must never read. The output buffer is four words and only two are written; the other two must keep their 0x9C poison. `execution_safety` is `authored_bounded`: the AIR has six CFG cycles -- two `elem_to_loc` walks bounded by `ndim` = 1, the block loop bounded by ceil(axis_size / 4*lsize) = 1, two four-element inner loops, and the two shuffle reductions bounded by log2(simd_size) = 5.

name: truncate-sixteen-halves-toward-zero-into-a-restrided-int4-window
rationale: The entry is a one-line forwarder into a helper that copies a half4 row-major window into an int4 buffer under a different stride, so this case fixes both strides apart and makes the conversion the only arithmetic. `stride_h` is read from field 6 of the 40-byte dims buffer -- note the GEP walks a ten-int type while the argument is declared `buffer_dims_and_strides`, and both agree that field 6 is byte 24 -- and `stride_h >> 2` is 2, so the guard `gid.x < sub_batch_rows * 2` is 6 and the 8-thread grid drops its last two threads. A surviving thread splits gid.x into row = gid.x / 2 and col = gid.x % 2, reads src at row * stride_h4 + col with stride_h4 = 5, and writes dst at col + row * 2 + sub_batch_offset_div4 with the offset 1. The two strides differ, so src indices 0, 1, 5, 6, 10, 11 land on dst indices 1 through 6: dst index 0 is below the offset and indices 7 upward are past the guard, and both keep their 0xCC poison. Every half is exactly representable and each names a rounding rule that must NOT be used: 3.5 and -3.5 become 3 and -3, so the conversion is not round-to-nearest; -1.0009765625 becomes -1, so it is not floor; 1 - 2^-11 and its negation both become 0, so it is truncation toward zero on both signs. -0.0 becomes 0, and 65504 and -65504 carry the half format's extreme finite magnitudes through a widening the int4 destination can hold exactly.

name: half4-exp-and-both-logarithms
rationale: air.exp.v4f16, air.log.v4f16 and air.log2.v4f16 are the highest-reach uncased symbols left: 360 corpus sources call all three, and every one of those hosts is a 262KB-plus cnnConvArray_* kernel gated behind function constants. This fixture asks the three symbols directly. Half exp/log is byte-authorable because at half width precise:: log/log2/exp are bit-identical to their fast:: spellings AND to widen-compute-narrow through float, over all 65536 half bit patterns -- so the variant MoltenVK's runtime compiler happens to pick, the thing that makes the half pow and trig families unauthorable, cannot move a byte here. Every input is exactly representable as a half, so the only rounding left is the function's own. The rows discriminate the three lowerings lane by lane rather than resting on exact anchors: at the input 2.0 exp answers 7.39 (0x4764), log answers 0.6934 (0x398c) and log2 answers 1.0 (0x3c00), so confusing any pair of them, or dropping a lane of the four-wide vector and leaving 0xABABABAB behind, moves the observed bytes. The exact anchors -- exp(0)=1, log(1)=0, log2(2^k)=k -- are present because they are the lanes a wrong implementation would still pass, which is why they are not the only lanes.

name: normal-pack-rounds-both-half-scales-before-the-narrowing-convert
rationale:
The fragment packs a world-space normal into one ushort: eight bits of x, seven of y and a sign bit for z. Each channel is scaled into a half and handed to air.round.f16 before the narrowing convert, so the case is a direct reading of that rounding. The only varying is a float3, which the harness fixes to float3(uv.x, uv.y, 0.5); the sixteen fragments of the leftmost column of a 16x16 target give sixteen distinct normals, and all sixteen packed words differ, so no texel can be satisfied by another's answer. Seventeen of the thirty-two scaled halves carry a fractional part at or above one half, so a lowering that truncated or floored instead of rounding would miss fourteen of the sixteen texels; the rest land below one half or on exact integers, where rounding must not move them. No fraction lands exactly on one half, so this pins the direction of rounding but not the tie rule; the away-from-zero tie is covered by the unit test on the widen-add-truncate sequence. z is 0.5 for every fragment, so the sign bit is zero throughout and records only that the comparison does not invert.

The column and the target size were chosen for tolerance. A fragment case cannot choose its varying: uv arrives through the rasterizer, and it is not bit-identical to (x + 0.5) / width computed in float64. Sweeping this same shader over all 64 fragments of an 8x8 target disagreed with an exact model at three of them, and each of the three is reconciled by a relative change of at most 7.3e-4 in the interpolated vector -- so that is the deviation this device actually produces, measured rather than assumed -- and measured end to end, so it bounds everything between the fragment's position and the stored word whatever the source. The reciprocal square root is not it: air.fast_rsqrt.f32 sits within one ULP of correctly rounded on this device, twenty-three of twenty-four arguments exact, which is four orders of magnitude below the deviation being guarded against. Every texel in this column survives a relative perturbation of 5.07e-3 in uv, a factor of 6.9 over the measured deviation. The half quantisation is what buys that: normalize's f32 result narrows to half before the scale, so a perturbation is discarded outright unless it straddles a half boundary.

name: unclamped-lod-at-four-scales
rationale: air.calculate_unclamped_lod_texture_2d (3 corpus sources) had no authored case and cannot have one in a kernel: it needs fragment implicit derivatives, the translator refuses it outside a fragment stage, and all three corpus sources that call it are fragment shaders. The coordinate is driven by position rather than by a varying, because a fragment case cannot choose its varyings and the uv that arrives through the rasteriser is not bit-exactly (x + 0.5) / W, while gl_FragCoord's derivative across a quad is exactly one pixel -- so the coordinate advances by exactly 1/16 per pixel and every LOD here is an exact integer rather than something interpolated. Four textures at four sizes turn that one derivative into four answers: the scale in texels per pixel is size/16, so the LODs are log2 of 1, 4, 1/4 and 2, that is 0, 2, -2 and 1. The negative one is the whole point of the symbol, since calculate_clamped_lod would answer 0 there. All 256 pixels answer the same four values, so the case is also a statement that the LOD does not drift across the target.
